body_html:
How to think about it

Unstable nuclei decay by emitting alpha (⁴₂He), beta (an electron or positron) or gamma radiation. In a nuclear equation the nucleon numbers and proton numbers balance on each side.

The half-life is the time for half the nuclei to decay. Fission splits heavy nuclei; fusion joins light nuclei. Both release energy because the products are more tightly bound; the lost mass becomes energy, E = mc².

Example

Iodine-131 (half-life 8 days): fraction left after 24 days?

24 ÷ 8 = 3 half-lives

(½)³

Answer: 1/8

Example

Energy from 1.0 g of mass?

E = 0.001 × (3.0 × 10⁸)²

Answer: 9.0 × 10¹³ J

Common mistakes

  • Thinking half-life means half the time for complete decay.
  • Forgetting that beta-minus decay raises the proton number by 1.
  • Saying gamma radiation changes the nucleon number.

faq.q: Why does a nucleus emit radiation?
faq.a: Its combination of protons and neutrons is unstable; decay moves it towards a more stable arrangement.

faq.q: Why can both fission and fusion release energy?
faq.a: In both, the products have a higher binding energy per nucleon than the reactants, so some mass is converted into energy.

items.q: Why does Australia's OPAL research reactor at Lucas Heights produce radioisotopes?
c: to generate most of the country's electricity
for nuclear medicine, such as technetium-99m for medical scans

items.q: What is nuclear fission?
c: a nucleus emits only gamma rays
a heavy nucleus such as uranium-235 splits into two smaller nuclei, releasing energy and neutrons
items.e: Fission is used in nuclear reactors.

items.q: A nucleus with atomic number 28 undergoes gamma decay. What is the new atomic number?
items.e: Gamma decay changes the atomic number by 0.

items.q: A nucleus with atomic number 49 undergoes alpha decay. What is the new atomic number?
items.e: Alpha decay changes the atomic number by −2.

items.q: What is mass defect?
c: the difference between the mass of a nucleus and the total mass of its separate nucleons
the mass of the neutrons only
the mass lost when an atom loses electrons
items.e: It is equivalent to the binding energy.

items.q: A nucleus with mass number 122 undergoes alpha decay. What is the new mass number?
items.e: Alpha decay changes the mass number by −4.

items.q: What is an alpha particle?
c: a helium-4 nucleus: 2 protons and 2 neutrons

items.q: What is a beta-minus particle?
c: a fast electron emitted when a neutron changes into a proton
items.e: The proton number goes up by 1.

items.q: A nucleus has 40 protons and 52 neutrons. It undergoes alpha decay. How many neutrons does the new nucleus have?
items.e: An alpha particle carries away 2 neutrons.

items.q: Why do fission and fusion both release energy?
c: the products have a higher binding energy per nucleon, so mass is converted to energy (E = mc²)

items.q: Which radiation needs several centimetres of lead to reduce it greatly?
Why is alpha radiation most dangerous inside the body?
c: it passes straight through the body
it is very ionising and all its energy is absorbed by nearby cells
it is stopped by skin outside the body, so it is safe inside
items.e: Outside the body skin stops it.

items.q: A nucleus has 86 protons and 86 neutrons. It undergoes alpha decay. How many neutrons does the new nucleus have?
items.e: An alpha particle carries away 2 neutrons.

items.q: Which unit measures the activity of a radioactive source?
Why is technetium-99m good for medical imaging?
c: it has a half-life of millions of years
it emits gamma rays that leave the body and has a short half-life (about 6 hours)
items.e: Short half-life means a low dose.

items.q: What is the half-life of a radioactive isotope?
c: the time for the mass of the sample to halve because of heat
half the time for all the nuclei to decay
the time for half the nuclei in a sample to decay
items.e: It is constant for each isotope.

items.q: Which nucleus has the highest binding energy per nucleon?
c: iron-56 (near the peak of the curve)
items.e: Nuclei lighter than iron can release energy by fusion; heavier ones by fission.

items.q: Which radiation is stopped by a sheet of paper?
items.e: Alpha is the most ionising and least penetrating.

items.q: What is a chain reaction?
c: neutrons from one fission cause further fissions
electrons cause atoms to ionise one after another
a reaction that needs no fuel
alpha particles join to make heavier nuclei
items.e: Control rods absorb neutrons to control the rate.
